facts.statement: Halisaurus auriculatus was described as a new species (sp. nov).
Halisaurus auriculatus lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian age.
Its type locality is the Dakhla Formation in Egypt.
The species is known from Egypt.
Halisaurus auriculatus is a valid species of mosasaur.
It belongs to the subfamily Halisaurinae within the mosasaur family.
facts.quote: A mosasaur belonging to the subfamily Halisaurinae; a species of Halisaurus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis placed H. auriculatus in a polytomy with H. hebae and the clade formed by H. arambourgi and H. platyspondylus.
facts.quote: H. auriculatus was recovered in a polytomy with H. hebae and the clade formed by H. arambourgi and H. platyspondylus.

facts.statement: The genus name Halisaurus means “ocean lizard”.
facts.quote: Halisaurus (“lagarto del océano”) es un género extinto de lagarto marino que pertenece a la familia Mosasauridae.

facts.statement: Halisaurus individuals measured about 3 to 4 metres (10 to 13 feet) in length, making them small compared with most other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Con una longitud de 3-4 m (10-13 pies) era pequeño comparado con la mayoría de los otros mosasaurios.

facts.statement: A BBC program suggested that Halisaurus hid in underwater caves to ambush small animals such as Hesperornis.
facts.quote: El programa sugirió que Halisaurus se ocultaba en las cuevas subacuáticas donde esperaba para atacar pequeños animales (como el Hesperornis).

facts.statement: The presence of two morphologically distinct halisaurine species in the Dakhla Shale implies that these mosasaurs practiced niche partitioning.
The genus Halisaurus lived from the Santonian to the Danian, approximately 85.7 to 61.66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Danian (85.7 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The description of Halisaurus auriculatus was published in the journal Acta Palaeontologica Polonica in 2026.
